title: Workflow Based on the Combination of Isotopic Tracer Experiments to Investigate Microbial Metabolism of Multiple Nutrient Sources
protocol: Prepare 500 mL of SM medium excluding the nitrogen source to be studied.
Pasteurize each medium in a 1 L flask at 100 °C for 10 min.
Weigh the appropriate amount of labeled molecule as specified in Table 1.
Dissolve the labeled molecule in the prepared medium.
Sterilize the medium using a disposable vacuum filtration system (cellulose acetate membrane, 0.22 µm).
Divide the medium between two pre-sterilized fermenters (250 mL) containing magnetic stirring bars and equipped with fermentation locks.
Place the fermentation flasks in an incubation room set at 28 °C for 1 night to heat them to 28 °C.
Grow S. cerevisiae strain in sterile tubes containing 10 mL of YPD medium at 28 °C with shaking (150 rpm) for 12 h.
Pipette 1 mL of YPD preculture and transfer it to 10 mL of SM medium in 15 mL sterile tubes.
Incubate the culture for 12 h at 28 °C with shaking (150 rpm).
Under laminar flow, collect a preculture aliquot and quantify the cell population using an electronic particle counter fitted with a 100 µm aperture.
Centrifuge the preculture (2,000 x g, 15 min, 4 °C) and suspend the pellet in sterile water to obtain a final concentration of 2.5 x 108 cells/mL.
Inoculate each fermenter with 1 mL of the cell suspension.
Install fermenters on the support guides placed on the 21-position stirring plates.
Set the stirring rate to 270 rpm.
Launch the robot-control application and click the "start assay" button.
Select a fermentation volume of 300 mL.
Right-click on the slot location and choose "enable" to activate fermenter monitoring.
Initialize the calculation software by clicking on the "Initialiser" button and validating with "ok".
Click on the "Start button" of the robot-control application to start weight acquisitions.
Sample from each fermenter when CO2 production reaches 5 g/L, 10 g/L, 40 g/L, and 90 g/L.
Centrifuge two 6 mL samples at 2,000 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Save and store the frozen supernatants in two aliquots at -80°C.
Wash pellets twice with 5 mL distilled water.
Store washed pellets at -80°C for isotopic enrichment measurements.
Harvest 10 mL of culture for dry weight determination.
Centrifuge two 10 mL samples at 2,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Wash the pellets twice with 10 mL distilled water.
Store washed pellets at -80°C for further analysis.
Dissolve 25 mg of (NH4)2SO4 in a 100 mL volumetric flask to prepare a standard ammonia solution (61.4 mg/L).
Perform a 1:2 dilution of samples taken before fermentation and at 5 g/L CO2 released.
Adjust the pH of diluted samples to approximately 8 with 1 M KOH.
Mix 100 μL of sample, distilled water or standard ammonia solution with 2 mL reagent 1 (ADP and glutamate dehydrogenase) and 500 μL reagent 2 (NADH).
Incubate the mixture for 15 min at room temperature.
Read NADH absorbance at 340 nm (A1).
Add 500 μL of reagent 3 to the mixture.
Incubate the sample for 20 min at room temperature.
Read the final NADH absorbance at 340 nm (A2).
Calculate ammonia concentration using the formula: Cammonia (g/L) = 0.083 x [(0.839 x A1 -A2)sample- (0.839 x A1 -A2)distilled water].
Check that the correct concentration is obtained with the standard solution.

Prepare a reference solution by adding 200 µL of a commercial mixture of neutral and acidic amino acids, 200 µL of a commercial mixture of basic amino acids, and 200 µL of 2.5 mM glutamine to 400 µL of 200 mM lithium citrate buffer, pH 2.2.
Treat the prepared reference solution as a sample for chromatographic analysis.
Add 200 μL of 25% (w/v) sulfosalicylic acid solution containing 2.5 mM norleucine to 800 μL of sample.
Incubate for 1 hour at 4 °C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 3,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22-μm pore-size nitrocellulose membrane using a syringe system.
In the programmer software, click on the button "Run" to begin LC analyses with an analyzer equipped with a cation-exchange column (lithium form).
Elute amino acids with successive lithium buffers to create both a pH gradient and a gradient in counter-ion concentration along with a temperature gradient.
Quantify nitrogen compounds after ninhydrin derivatization by spectrophotometric detection at 570 nm for purple coloration and 440 nm for yellow coloration.
Perform single-point internal calibration using the reference solution and norleucine as an internal standard to calculate amino acid concentrations in samples with manufacturer's software.
Filter 10 mL of culture through a nitrocellulose filter (pore size 0.45 μm) that is pre-weighed in an aluminum cup, using a vacuum device.
Wash the filtered sample twice with 50 mL of distilled water.
Place the filter in the aluminum cup and dry in a heat oven at 105 °C for 48 h.
Reweigh the filter in the cup after drying.
Calculate the weight difference of the filter.
Extract proteins by adding 1 mL of DMSO solution (50% v/v) to frozen pellets.
Incubate protein extracts at 105 °C for 1 h in a dry heat oven.
Quantify the protein content in the DMSO extracts using BCA assay.
Prepare an oxidized extract by suspending the cell pellet in 200 μL of performic acid (90% formic acid, 10% hydrogen peroxide).
Incubate for 4 h at 4 °C.
Stop the reaction by adding 33.6 mg sodium sulfate.
Add 800 µL of 6N HCl to cell pellets or oxidized extract.
Incubate the sample in a hermetically sealed glass tube for 16 h at 110 °C in a dry heat oven.
Add 200 µL of 2.5 mM norleucine to the dried extract.
Remove HCl with a stream of nitrogen.
Wash the dried extract twice with 800 µL of distilled water and then with 800 µL of ethanol.
Take up in 800 µL of 200 mM lithium acetate buffer, pH 2.2.
Add 160 µL of a commercial solution of hydrolyzed amino acids to 840 µL of 200 mM lithium acetate buffer, pH 2.2, that contains 625 µM methionine sulfone, 625 µM cysteic acid, and 625 µM norleucine.
Determine the relative concentrations of amino acids within proteins using the chromatographic method described.
Calculate the weight percentage of each amino acid by dividing its measured amount (mg/L) by the total amount of amino acids measured in the protein extract (sum in mg/L).

Multiply this percentage by the concentration of proteins in the culture (mg/L), which is the product between the protein content of the biomass and the dry weight, to assess the concentration of each proteinogenic amino acid in the culture (mg/L).
Hydrolyze cell pellets by adding 1.2 mL of 6 M HCl and incubating for 16 h at 105 °C.
Centrifuge the sample at 3,000 x g for 5 min to remove cellular debris.
Distribute the supernatant into six 400 µL fractions in open glass tubes.
Dry the fractions in a heat oven at 105 °C until they reach the consistency of syrup (4-5 h).
Dissolve the dried hydrolysate in 200 µL of 20 mM HCl.
Add 133 µL of pyridine:ethanol (1:4) to the dissolved hydrolysate.
Add 50 µL of ethylchloroformate (ECF) to derivatize the amino acids and wait until all CO2 has been released.
Transfer the mixture to centrifuge tubes containing 500 µL of dichloromethane.
Vortex the tubes for 10 s and centrifuge them for 4 min at 10,000 x g.
Collect the lower organic phase with a Pasteur pipet and transfer it to GC vials that contain conical glass inserts.
Dissolve the dried hydrolysate in 50 µL of methanol and 200 µL of acetonitrile.
Add 300 µL of N,N-dimethylformamide dimethyl acetal (DMFDMA).
Vortex the tube and transfer the samples to GC autosampler vials that contain conical glass inserts.
Suspend the hydrolysate in 200 µL of acetonitrile.
Add 200 µL of BSTFA.
Incubate the mixture hermetically closed in a glass tube at 135 °C for 4 hours.
Transfer the extract directly to GC vials.
Analyze samples using a gas chromatograph equipped with an autosampler injector and coupled to a mass spectrometer.
Create the sample list by clicking "Sample Log Table" in the "Sequence" menu.
Start the injections by clicking the "Run" button.
Set the temperature of the inlet at 230 °C and that of the source at 250 °C for ECF derivatives analysis.
Inject 1 µL of samples with a split ratio of 3:1 using helium as the mobile phase with a flow of 1.2 mL/min.
Gradually increase the oven temperature starting from 130 °C for 3 minutes, then at a gradient of 15 °C/min to 260 °C, and maintain it at 260 °C for 20 minutes.
Use helium as the mobile phase with a constant flow of 1.2 mL/min.
Set the temperature of the inlet at 230 °C for DMFDMA derivatives.
Set the temperature of the source at 250 °C for DMFDMA derivatives.
Program the autosampler to inject 1 µL of samples with a split ratio of 3:1.
Run the analyses, gradually increasing the oven temperature as follows:
Increase from 60 °C to 130 °C over 8.5 min at 20 °C/min for DMFDMA derivatives.
Increase from 130 °C to 260 °C over 7.25 min at 4 °C/min for DMFDMA derivatives.
Maintain the temperature at 260 °C for 10 min for DMFDMA derivatives.
Set the temperature of the inlet at 275 °C for BSTFA derivatives.
Set the temperature of the source at 300 °C for BSTFA derivatives.
Inject a sample (1 µL) in SCAN mode with positive electron impact ionization at 70 eV for each derivatized sample.
Take note of the retention time of each amino acid.
Define the time windows throughout the chromatogram based on retention times.
Identify and include the characteristic selected ions for each amino acid from Table 3.
Include this information in the SIM detection program.
Run the analyses in SIM mode with positive electron impact ionization at 70 eV.
Record a cluster of intensities for each amino acid corresponding to its different mass isotopomers.
Process the data using dedicated software to correct for natural labeling and calculate the isotopic enrichment.
Add 10 µL of deuterated internal standards to 5 mL of supernatant (final concentration: 100 µg/L).
Add 1 mL of dichloromethane, tightly close the tubes, and shake on a rocking platform for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 5 min and collect the organic lower phase in a glass tube.
Repeat the dichloromethane extraction.
Dry the organic extract over 500 mg of anhydrous sodium sulfate.
Collect the liquid phase with a Pasteur pipet.
Concentrate the extract by a factor of four under nitrogen flux.
Transfer the concentrated extract to a GC autosampler vial.
Equip the gas chromatograph with a 30 m x 0.25 mm fused silica capillary column with 0.25 μm film thickness.
Apply a constant helium flow of 1.0 mL/min.
Hold the injector and the transfer line at 250 °C.
Inject 2 µL of sample with a split ratio of 10:1.
Hold the oven temperature for 3 min at 40 °C.
Increase the temperature by 4 °C/min up to 220 °C.
Hold the oven at 220 °C for 20 min.
Set the mass spectrometer source temperature at 230 °C.
Set the mass spectrometer quadrupole temperature at 150 °C.
Record the mass spectra in Selected Ion Monitoring (SIM) mode with positive electron impact ionization at 70 eV.
Use an external 7-point calibration to quantify the concentrations of volatile molecules from the sums of the intensities of the corresponding ion cluster.
Prepare stock solutions of each compound (10 g/L) in 100% ethanol.
Mix stock solutions to prepare standard solutions for ethyl esters, acetates, alcohols, and acids.
Dilute different amounts of the standard solutions in a 12% hydroalcoholic solution containing 5 g/L tartaric acid with pH adjusted to 3.3 to prepare calibration solutions.
Correct for the natural labeling of the intensities of each ion cluster.
Calculate the isotopic enrichment of volatile compounds using dedicated software.
Enter raw data values into spreadsheets shown in Tables 5, 6, 7, and 8.
Express raw data values in mM.
Convert concentrations to mg/L by multiplying by molecular weight.
Convert millimolar concentration of proteinogenic amino acids to mg N/L by considering atomic mass of nitrogen (14 u) and number of nitrogen atoms provided by catabolism.
Calculate the mass percentage of each amino acid in proteins by dividing its amount in mg/L in the hydrolysate by the total amount of amino acids.
Calculate means, standard deviations, and standard errors of the mean from independent experiments.

Calculate the proteinogenic concentration for each amino acid by multiplying the percentage of the amino acid in proteins by the protein fraction in the biomass and the dry weight content in the medium.
Using spreadsheets, calculate the labeled and unlabeled fractions of nitrogen present in the proteinogenic amino acids from their total concentrations and isotopic enrichments.
For each amino acid, determine the labeled fraction as the product of its total concentration and its isotopic enrichment.
Determine the unlabeled fraction for each amino acid by subtracting the labeled amount from the total amount.
Sum the total amount of nitrogen in Ala, Gly, Val, Asp, Phe, Leu, Ile, Thr, Ser, Pro, Lys, His, Glu and Arg (in mg N/L).
Divide the total amount of nitrogen contained in proteins by the sum of nitrogen in quantified amino acids to determine the fraction of total nitrogen in proteins.
Calculate the labeled fraction of nitrogen from arginine, glutamine, or ammonium in mg N/L.
Sum the labeled-nitrogen fractions of quantified proteinogenic amino acids (Ala, Gly, Val, Asp, Phe, Leu, Ile, Thr, Ser, Pro, Lys, His, Glu, and Arg).
Divide the total labeled nitrogen by the total amount of nitrogen in the quantified proteinogenic amino acids.
Assess the contribution of the 3 most abundant amino acids to the intracellular pool of nitrogen for de novo biosynthesis using data from 13C and 15N isotope tracer experiments.
Deduct the part derived from direct incorporation of consumed compounds (from 13C experiments) from the total amount of Val, Leu, Ile, or Thr.

Subtract the part de novo synthetized using nitrogen from the three major sources from the total amount of proteinogenic amino acids to assess the fraction synthesized using other amino acid nitrogen.
Calculate the ratio of nitrogen provided by Gln, Arg, and NH4+ (sum in mM) to the total amount of proteinogenic amino acids (in mM).

Calculate the labeled and unlabeled fractions of proteinogenic amino acids from concentrations expressed in mM and isotopic enrichments obtained during experiments with 13C-labeled Leu, Val, Ile, or Thr.
Calculate the labeled and unlabeled fractions of volatile compounds from concentrations expressed in mM and isotopic enrichments obtained during experiments with 13C-labeled Leu, Val, Ile, or Thr.
